name: The Way and the Dharma: Asian Thought
description: Confucius, the Buddha, Mahavira, Laozi-era Daoists and their heirs: the schools of China and India that still shape how hundreds of millions of people think.

checkpoints.name: Roots of two traditions
checkpoints.note: Vedic ritual grew into the ideas later called Hinduism, while in the sixth and fifth centuries BCE Mahavira and the Buddha taught paths out of suffering in India, and Confucius taught ethical living and good government in China.

checkpoints.name: The hundred schools
checkpoints.note: During the Warring States period Chinese thinkers argued over how to rule and live: Mencius and the Confucians, the Mohists, the Legalists and the Daoists of the Tao Te Ching. In India, Ashoka promoted Buddhist ethics and Nagarjuna wrote on emptiness.

checkpoints.name: Monasteries and commentary
checkpoints.note: Nalanda became a great Buddhist centre of learning, colossal Buddhas were carved at Bamiyan, Shankara argued for non-dual Vedanta, and the monk Kukai brought esoteric Buddhism to Japan.

checkpoints.name: Reform and new paths
checkpoints.note: Zhu Xi and Wang Yangming reshaped Confucian thought, Nichiren taught in Japan, Guru Nanak founded Sikhism, and the 14th Dalai Lama became a widely known teacher of Tibetan Buddhism.
